mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying, exalted is He, {تِلْكَ آيَات الْكتاب الْمُبين}: تلك is in the position of the nominative in the sense "this is that" (هَذِه تِلْكَ), and آيات is a badal (substitute) for it. In ordinary speech تلك may be in the position of the accusative by نتلوا, and you would put آيات in the accusative as a badal for تلك.

mekki-muskil:4-4.t:
His saying {وَجعل أَهلهَا شيعًا}: two objects of جعل, because it has the meaning of صيّر ("to make into"). If it has the meaning of خلق ("to create"), it takes one object, as in His saying {وَجعل الظُّلُمَات والنور}. And خلق, when it has the meaning of صيّر, takes two objects, as in {ثمَّ خلقنَا النُّطْفَة علقَة}; and if it has the meaning of "to originate, to bring into being", it takes one object, as in {خلق الله السَّمَاوَات}.
His saying {قُرَّة عين}: nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "he is a comfort of the eye for me". It may also be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar (predicate) is لا تقتلوه. It may also be accusative by an implied verb which لا تقتلوه explains, its implied form being "leave a comfort of the eye; do not kill him".

mekki-muskil:10-10.t: His saying {لَوْلَا أَن ربطنا على قَلبهَا}: أن is in the position of the nominative and the apodosis (jawāb) is omitted. Its explanation has already been given.

mekki-muskil:14-14.t: His saying {بلغ أشده}: according to Sībawayh its pattern is أفعل, and in his view it is the plural of شدّة, like نعمة and أنعم. Others said it is the plural of شدّ, like قِدّ and أقدّ. It is also said that it is a singular, though in the language there is no singular noun on the pattern أفعُل without the tāʾ marbūṭa except أصبع in some of its dialectal forms.

mekki-muskil:15-15.t: His saying {وَهَذَا من عدوه}: i.e. "of his enemies". Its meaning is that when an onlooker looked at the two of them, he would say that.

mekki-muskil:18-18.t:
His saying {خَائفًا}: the khabar (predicate) of أصبح; or, if you wish, as a ḥāl (circumstantial), with في المدينة as the khabar.
His saying {فَإِذا الَّذِي استنصره بالْأَمْس يستصرخه}: الذي is a mubtadaʾ (subject), what follows it is its ṣila (relative clause), and يستصرخه is the khabar. It is also permissible for إذا to be the khabar and يستصرخه a ḥāl.
His saying تمشي: in the position of a ḥāl from {إِحْدَاهمَا}, governed by جاءت. {على استحياء} is in the position of a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in تمشي, governed by تمشي. على استحياء may also be in the position of a ḥāl placed first, from the latent pronoun in قالت, governed by قالت; the first is better. On the second view it is good to pause at تمشي; on the first view it is not good to pause except at على استحياء.

mekki-muskil:28-28.t:
His saying {قَالَ ذَلِك بيني وَبَيْنك}: ذلك is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and what follows it is its khabar (predicate); its meaning according to Sībawayh is "that is between us".
His saying {أَيّمَا الْأَجَليْنِ قضيت}: you make أيا accusative by قضيت, and ما is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, and you put الأجلين in the genitive because أي is annexed to it. Ibn Kaysān said: ما is in the position of the genitive because أي is annexed to it, and it is indefinite, and الأجلين is a badal (substitute) for ما. He said the same about His saying {فبمَا رَحْمَة من الله}: that رحمة is a badal for ما. He used to take pains not to make anything in the Qur'an redundant, and would devise for it an interpretation that takes it out of redundancy.

mekki-muskil:30-30.t: His saying {أَن يَا مُوسَى}: أن is in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition, i.e. "with (بأن) 'O Moses'".

mekki-muskil:31-31.t:
His saying {أَن ألق عصاك}: conjoined to it.
His saying {مُدبرا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); likewise the position of His saying ولم يعقب is also in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.

mekki-muskil:32-32.t:
His saying {من الرهب}: attached to (mutaʿalliq) ولّى, i.e. "he turned back fleeing out of fear".
His saying {فذانك}: it is the dual of the nominative ذا, and it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). The alif of ذا is elided because the alif of the dual entered upon it. Whoever reads it with the nūn doubled made the doubling a compensation for the loss of the alif of ذا. It is also said that whoever doubles it based it only on the dialect of those who say ذلك in the singular; when he made it dual, he kept the lām after the nūn of the dual, then assimilated the lām into the nūn according to the rule of assimilating the second into the first. The rule is always to assimilate the first into the second, unless some cause prevents that, in which case the second is assimilated into the first. The cause that prevented assimilating the first into the second here is that, had that been done, a doubled lām would have stood in the place of the nūn that indicates the dual, and the form of the dual would have changed; so the second was assimilated into the first for that reason, and it became a doubled nūn. It has also been said that when he made it dual he kept the lām that is in ذلك before the nūn, then assimilated the first into the second according to the principles of assimilation, and it became a doubled nūn. It is also said that the nūn in these vague nouns (al-mubhamāt) is doubled only to distinguish between the nūn that is a compensation for a vowel and tanwīn, or for tanwīn — something present or implied in the singular — and that which is not present in the singular. It is also said that it was doubled to distinguish between the nūn that is dropped in annexation and the nūn that is never dropped in annexation, which is the nūn of the dual of the vague noun. The same is the reason for doubling the nūn in اللذان and اللذين and هذان and the like.

mekki-muskil:34-34.t: His saying {ردْءًا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in أرسله. Likewise يصدقني is a ḥāl in the reading of whoever puts it in the nominative, or a naʿt (adjective) of ردء; whoever puts it in the jussive does so as the answer to the request.

mekki-muskil:42-42.t:
His saying {وَيَوْم الْقِيَامَة هم من المقبوحين}: يوم is accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa), as though He said "and We made a curse follow them in this world, and a curse of the Day of Resurrection"; then the (second) curse was omitted because the first indicates it, and يوم stood in its place and took its accusative. You may also put اليوم in the accusative by conjoining it to the position of في هذه الدنيا, as (the poet) said:
.. إِذا مَا تلاقينا من الْيَوْم أَو غَدا ...
(When we meet, today or tomorrow.)
يوم may also be accusative as an adverb of المقبوحين, i.e. "and they will be among the despised on the Day of Resurrection", with the adverb then placed first.

mekki-muskil:43-43.t: His saying بصائر وَهدى وَرَحْمَة: all accusative as aḥwāl (circumstantial expressions) from الكتاب.

mekki-muskil:46-46.t: His saying {وَلَكِن رَحْمَة من رَبك}: الرحمة is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) according to al-Akhfash, meaning "but your Lord had mercy on you, O Muhammad, with a mercy". According to al-Zajjāj it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "but He did that for mercy", i.e. for the sake of mercy. Al-Kisāʾī said it is the khabar (predicate) of an implied كان, meaning "but that was a mercy from your Lord". In ordinary speech the nominative is permissible, meaning "but it is a mercy".

mekki-muskil:58-58.t: His saying {بطرت معيشتها}: المعيشة is accusative according to al-Māzinī by omission of the preposition, its implied form being "it exulted in its livelihood" (بطرت في معيشتها). Al-Farrāʾ said it is accusative as specification (tafsīr, i.e. tamyīz), but this is far-fetched, because it is definite and tamyīz can only be indefinite. It is also said that it is accusative by بطرت, with بطرت meaning "was ignorant of", i.e. "it was ignorant of gratitude for its livelihood", then the muḍāf was omitted.

mekki-muskil:68-68.t: His saying {وَرَبك يخلق مَا يَشَاء ويختار مَا كَانَ}: the second ما is for negation and has no grammatical position. Some scholars — al-Ṭabarī and others — said it is in the position of the accusative by يختار. That is not good in i'rab, because there is no returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) in the sentence referring to ما. It is also far-fetched in meaning and in creed, because its being for negation requires that it cover all things — that they came about by the decree of Allah and His choice, and that the servant has nothing in them other than his acquisition (iktisāb), by a decree from Allah. Whereas if you make ما in the position of the accusative by يختار, it does not cover all things as being chosen by Allah; it only requires that He chooses that in which they have the choice, nothing else, and negates that in which they have no choice — and this is the doctrine of the Qadariyya and the Muʿtazila. So ما being for negation is more fitting in meaning, more correct in interpretation, better in creed and stronger in Arabic. Do you not see that if you made ما in the position of the accusative, its pronoun in كان would be its ism (noun), and it would be necessary to put الخيرة in the accusative — yet no one has read it so? It has been said in the interpretation of this verse that its meaning is: "and your Lord, O Muhammad, creates what He wills and chooses for His friendship (walāya) and His message whomever He wants". Then He began by negating choice from the polytheists, and that they have no power, saying "they have no choice", i.e. friendship, the message and other things are not by their choice nor by their wish. And Allah knows best what He means by that. This verse needs much more extensive treatment than this, and what we have pointed to is sufficient.

mekki-muskil:76-76.t: His saying {مَا إِن مفاتحه لتنوء}: ما is in the position of the accusative by آتيناه as a second object, and إنّ with its ism (noun) and khabar (predicate), and what is connected to it up to His saying أولي القوة, is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. The singular of أولي is ذي.

mekki-muskil:82-82.t: His saying ويكأن الله: its origin is وي, separate from the kāf. Sībawayh said, citing al-Khalīl, about its meaning: the people became aware, or were made aware, and said وي; it is a word that the remorseful says when he shows his remorse. Al-Farrāʾ said: وي is joined to the kāf, and its origin is ويلك أن الله ("woe to you, that Allah…"); then the lām was elided and the kāf joined to أن. There is something far-fetched in this, in meaning and in i'rab, because the people were not addressing anyone, because eliding the lām from this is not known, and because أن would then have had to be with kasra, since nothing requires its fatḥa.

mekki-muskil:88-88.t:
His saying {كل شَيْء هَالك إِلَّا وَجهه}: الوجه is accusative by exception. In ordinary speech the nominative is permissible in the sense of an adjective, as though He said "other than His Face" (غير وجهه), as (the poet) said:
... وكل أَخ مفارقه أَخُوهُ ... لعمر أَبِيك إِلَّا الفرقدان ...
(And every brother is parted from by his brother — by your father's life — except the two Farqad stars.)
i.e. "other than the two Farqad stars", so غير is an adjective of كل; such is the permissibility (of the nominative) in the verse.
